agree.reason: The plain terms and the open admission about the hours will earn some trust. Still, a long-serving teller who doesn't want phone work gets little reason to choose the center over a severance cheque and a job search.

honest.reason: Every number matches the brief and the 'make work better' claim is softened to 'many of us, though not in every way'. The only overreach is the unsupported line that a dedicated team means 'members reach us sooner'.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are copied rather than worked out: it never turns the severance into a concrete example such as 20 weeks after 10 years, and it never compares the 12-hour center day with a person's actual shift length.

right_comparison.reason: It uses the 44% drop and the 60% rise to show the trend behind keeping the branches open, and it states the leave option plainly. It doesn't say what keeping the branches would mean as visits keep falling.

qualification.reason: The only hedge is a vague 'not in every way for every person'. The reader needs dates and numbers they can check, such as a deadline to decide, when shift schedules will be set and how often they rotate, and none are given.

objections.reason: It names the hours as a real cost, but it skips the main objection that these staff don't want phone work beyond one line about transferable skills. It also ignores the two weeks of rumours and the loss of a branch where many have worked for over ten years.

fit.reason: It's a clear email from the COO with a useful bulleted section, a little over the 400 words asked for, and appropriately addressed to all staff.
